what: Manual single-bin reset approved by the owner on 2026-11-10. Two gf_correction_bin rows deleted from potomac_observations: the 12000-25000 steady flow bin and its paired stage bin. Both were created by one validation at 2026-10-13T07:00:18Z (a rising-limb miss labelled steady, on a row where the 120 percent ceiling bound).
why: One observation of +9,743 cfs. Blended with the hierarchical fallback it subtracted about 2,680 cfs from any steady estimate in the 12,000-25,000 band, in the unsafe (under-read) direction. See analysis/pulse-audit-2026-10/REPORT.md, problem 9.

before.hash_recipe: md5(string_agg(gauge_id || '|' || data::text, E'\n' order by gauge_id)) over observation_type = 'gf_correction_bin'

undo: Re-insert the two rows above (observation_type, gauge_id, data). A missing row is read as an empty bin, which is the state that held before 2026-10-13.
verified: Independent verifier, 2026-11-10 17:30Z: 28 rows remain, hash of the other 28 rows identical to the before-hash, live API shows the bin empty, real getGFCorrection for 12000-25000 steady returns 911.93 (was 2678.14 with the bin in place).
known_side_effects: The documented identity sum(flow bin counts) == validValidations == binWriteSuccesses is now off by one on purpose: flow bins sum to 439, both counters read 440. The counters were NOT decremented (that would be a second production write and they also feed avgErrorPercent). Anyone using the identity to look for lost bin writes (diagnostics panel, scripts/recover-bins.js) must subtract this one deliberate deletion.
The 2026-10-13 observation still counts in avgErrorPercent, stageValidations and sumAbsStageError. The delete did not touch those, and re-inserting the rows would not change them.

The next validation in this band and state creates a fresh one-observation bin seeded at its raw error, blended at weight 1/5. The reset removes the bad observation; it does not change how thin bins behave (see report problem 9).
